subject: [PATCH 1/3] mm: don't PTE-batch a swap-in over a hardware-poisoned subpage

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo raised concerns that scanning every page in a folio for HWPoison could be costly, and questioned why we're swapping out folios containing HWPoison pages instead of migrating away from them.
reviews.raw_body:
Hm, isn't scanning every single page in the folio potentially quite costly
here?  I thought the point of batching was to improve performance overall?

It seems broken to have stuff potentially interact with hwpoison but then
to only set the folio-level flag much later?

Also why are we swapping out folios containing hwpoison pages? Shouldn't we
migrate away from the hwpoison? :) (I'm not really familiar with the hw
poison stuff)

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2, but did not provide a clear indication of whether this change will be made in the current patch series or a future one.

Author acknowledged that swapping in requires checking every subpage and accepted the trade-off of added cost for correctness.

The author addressed Lorenzo's concern about PG_has_hwpoisoned being set after a THP split, explaining that it only gets set once the folio reference is held and get_hwpoison_page() gives up if it can't get a reference. However, they acknowledged that this doesn't cover the case of a large folio briefly off the LRU, which can still be mapped afterwards.

The author addressed Lorenzo's concern that memory_failure() can leave a folio flag clear, allowing a poisoned subpage to be mapped without being faulted. The author explained the issue occurs when get_hwpoison_page() fails for a folio off the LRU and noted that memory_failure() should split the folio and isolate the bad page in such cases. They also suggested adding an additional check for anon folios before checking for HWPoison.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Lorenzo,

Thanks for the reviews!

---

Swapping in requires checking every subpage, so there would be a cost.
I guess trading it off for correctness :(

---

PG_has_hwpoisoned lives in the second page, so memory_failure() only
sets it once it holds a folio reference, otherwise it could race with a
THP split. If get_hwpoison_page() can't get a reference,
memory_failure() gives up with only the subpage marked. The comment
above folio_set_has_hwpoisoned() in memory_failure() says that is fine:

  Don't need care about the above error handling paths for
  get_hwpoison_page() since they handle either free page
  or unhandlable page.

But a large folio that is briefly off the LRU, e.g. isolated by
reclaim, takes those paths too and can still be mapped afterwards.

---

The error hits a folio that is already in the swap
cache, e.g. while reclaim has it off the LRU to write it out, and
get_hwpoison_page() fails for any folio that is off the LRU. Normally
memory_failure() would split the folio and isolate the bad page (for
an uncorrected error there is nothing to migrate; that is soft
offline). Here it does neither, and the folio stays in the swap cache
with only the subpage marked.

While looking at this I also noticed that the fallback drops a freshly
read (not yet anon) folio from the swap cache and frees it with the
poisoned page in it. We should actually actually also check folio_test_anon()
before checking folio_has_any_hwpoisoned_page().

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan suggested replacing the newly introduced folio_has_any_hwpoisoned_page() function with a call to existing page_range_has_hwpoisoned() from mm/huge_memory.c, citing similarity between the two functions.

Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a subpage is hardware-poisoned but the folio-level PG_has_hwpoisoned flag is not set yet, and suggested adding a check for this condition in do_swap_page()
reviews.raw_body:
It looks almost the same as page_range_has_hwpoisoned() in mm/huge_memory.c.
Maybe change the function to call page_range_has_hwpoisoned() instead.

---

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch prevents the Linux kernel from batching swap-in operations over a hardware-poisoned subpage. The existing check for PageHWPoison() only looks at the faulting page, but the large-folio batching path maps the rest of the folio without checking other subpages. This can lead to a poisoned subpage being mapped and not triggering a fault. To fix this, the patch adds a new function folio_has_any_hwpoisoned_page() that scans all subpages for HWPoison(), and uses it in do_swap_page() to skip batching when a poisoned subpage is found.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) suggested avoiding an additional helper function for checking hardware-poisoned pages, instead recommending to reuse existing helpers that test the large-folio bit. He also mentioned that the memory-failure code is prone to races and needs a long-term solution.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, we don't really want another helper to check for hwpoison.

If we race with concurrent hwpoison, bad luck. The slapped on memory-failure
code is full of races. That needs a proper long-term solution, not more pain to
core-mm.

So let's please try reusing existing helpers that test the large-folio bit.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo noted that the patch's optimization to check every page of a folio for HWPoison instead of relying on the folio-level flag may have unintended consequences, as it increases the cost of swap-in operations for all pages, not just the poisoned one.

Reviewer Lorenzo raised concerns that the patch's optimization may be overly broad, and suggested limiting the scan for hardware-poisoned subpages to only when a poisoned subpage is detected.
reviews.raw_body:
(we don't say subpage apparently :)

Yeah but the cost is now paid by literally everybody...

And...

---

...now you're narrowing this cost to literally a vague edge case.

Can we not just do the scan _only in this case_?

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo pointed out that the patch is overly cautious and may unnecessarily skip batching for large folios, even when no subpage is poisoned, citing Usama's reply as justification.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah exactly. See Usama's reply - it really does narrow into a weird edge
case. Scan there if you want to scan at all.

Otherwise tough luck yes.
